Nobody has to sit on the laundry room floor watching the dryer spin. You start it, go make lunch, and come back when it buzzes.

In software, "make this async" usually means: when a slow step starts (like sending an email, building a report, or waiting on another service), let the rest of the product keep going instead of standing still until that step finishes, then handle the result when it arrives. It doesn't make the slow step itself any faster, and someone still has to decide what happens if it finishes late or fails.

Which part of the product does "this" refer to? That changes what the work actually involves.

input: In this hypothetical spreadsheet tool, a query specifies the requested rows and columns. The tool returns a separate result and leaves the source cells unchanged. The query must use the supported syntax; an invalid query returns an error. No timing guarantee or list of supported operations is given.
output:
You can ask a friend to read you just the birthdays off the family calendar, and the calendar is still hanging on the fridge exactly as it was.

Here's how it works in this hypothetical tool. You write a query that says which rows and which columns you want. The tool runs it and hands back a separate result containing that selection. The source cells you queried stay unchanged, so reading data this way doesn't edit your spreadsheet.

The query has to be written in the tool's supported syntax. If it isn't valid, you get an error instead of a result, so a typo or an unsupported form won't quietly return partial data. It just fails.

A few things the description leaves open:

- It doesn't list which operations are supported, so you can't assume things like filtering, sorting, joining, or calculations are available. Check the tool's own documentation before relying on any of them.
- It gives no timing guarantee, so there's no promise about how fast a query returns, on small sheets or large ones.
- It only says the source cells are unchanged by a query. It doesn't say what happens to the separate result if the source changes later, so don't assume the result stays in sync.
